title: Analyst, Compliance
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.

Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.

This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.

Job Description

Position Overview
Invenergy’s Compliance team develops, maintains, and communicates company governance, delivers targeted training and awareness programs, and provides ongoing guidance to ensure Invenergy operates with integrity and conducts business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations. The team identifies and manages compliance risks through due diligence, risk assessments, monitoring, testing, and internal controls in key areas including political compliance, anti-corruption and FCPA compliance, data privacy and protection, third-party risk management, and other regulatory and governance obligations.

Invenergy is seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Compliance Analyst to provide broad programmatic, analytical, and project support across the Compliance team.  This role will assist Compliance workstream leads with their initiatives, recurring activities, and additional priorities; help maintain organized and reliable processes; and collaborate with team members and business stakeholders to support an effective compliance program. This role will report to Invenergy’s Director of Compliance in Chicago, IL.

Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays.

Responsibilities

- Assist Compliance leads with program activities, including intake, review, research, monitoring, documentation, tracking, reporting, and recordkeeping.

- Respond to routine inquiries and coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to collect information, advance open items, and communicate compliance requirements clearly to varied audiences.

- Support Compliance leads with work stream project management execution, including the coordination of meetings, action items, timelines, and documentation for initiatives.

- Manage multiple assignments and provide timely, organized follow-through on recurring and ad hoc work.

- Provide flexible assistance across Compliance as business, legal, regulatory, compliance, and team priorities evolve.

- Support Compliance Lead with compliance operations such as policy management, compliance training and communication administration

- Support with risk assessments, due diligence, control reviews, testing, monitoring, and related documentation.

- Assist with political compliance activities, including processing donation and contribution requests, coordinating reviews and approvals, and maintaining required documentation and records.

- Collect, organize, and analyze information used to identify, evaluate, track, and report compliance risks.

- Support routine compliance reviews, research, monitoring, and other program activities.

- Compile and analyze information to prepare metrics, summaries, reports, and management updates.

- Help identify and implement opportunities to improve processes, strengthen controls, and use approved tools and technology more effectively.

- Help coordinate mitigation activities, maintain risk and action-item follow ups with stakeholders.

Minimum Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree

- 2+ years of relevant experience in compliance, legal, risk, governance, business operations, or a related field.

- Proficiency and experience with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, or other approved tools to analyze data, and prepare management-ready reporting.

- High attention to detail, sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to manage multiple priorities.

- Strong analytical, organizational, research, communication, and project coordination skills.

- Experience working cross-functionally with business stakeholders to gather and validate information, support remediation, evaluate process improvements, and communicate practical recommendations.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, attention to detail, and ability to translate complex information into clear, actionable insights for varied audiences.

- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

- Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Base Pay

$ 75,000.00 - $87,000.00 USD Annual
Bonus: 15%

The base pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target salary for the position. Invenergy considers a number of factors when determining base pay offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education and skills.

In addition to base pay, the total annual compensation package may also include eligibility to participate in our bonus program(s) which are designed to reward individual and company performance. Your recruiter can share more about bonus eligibility for this position during the hiring process.

Invenergy offers a variety of other benefits including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401k, paid time off, etc.

Invenergy LLC is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, among other things, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, status as a protected veteran, or disability.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to distill complex ideas and present to executive-level audiences.

- Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build credibility across teams and functions.

title: Manager, Electrical Engineering - Thermal
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.

Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.

This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.

Job Description

Position Overview
As a Manager, Thermal Electrical Engineering, you will lead and develop a team of engineers responsible for the electrical engineering, procurement support, and construction/commissioning support of cutting-edge Thermal generation projects (natural gas combustion turbines, combined cycle power plants, and related facilities). You will be primarily responsible for managing internal engineering resources and overseeing selected Engineering Firms to complete final detailed design packages for projects to be built. The electrical systems of these projects typically include large turbine generators, isophase bus duct, medium voltage and low voltage auxiliary systems (switchgear, breakers, MCCs), generator step-up transformers (GSUs), switchyard equipment, and high/extra-high voltage transmission interconnections to the grid.

Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays.

Responsibilities:
Electrical Engineering Management Responsibilities

- Manage up to 2 or 3 engineers; provide day-to-day technical guidance on issues encountered during engineering design, construction, commissioning, and placed-in-service activities.

- Conduct regular meetings with the assigned team, supervise project assignments and priorities, and perform performance reviews and coaching for team members.

- Responsible for achieving assigned goals for the team and department, including quality, schedule, and cost objectives for electrical deliverables.

- Support upper management with strategic planning, resource planning, and defining goals for the Thermal Electrical Engineering team.

- Develop and maintain standard designs, processes, and procedures for Thermal Electrical Engineering (e.g., BOP standards, switchyard and MV/LV auxiliary design templates).

- Implement industry best practices and incorporate project lessons learned across the team to continuously improve quality and execution.

- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of industry technology through training, conferences, and engagement with OEMs and EPC partners.

Electrical Engineering and Projects’ Technical Responsibility

- Assist in developing project-specific construction, engineering, and equipment specifications for thermal generation electrical systems (turbine-generator, isophase bus, MV/LV auxiliaries, protective relaying, station service, and switchyard).

- Assist in the development of new projects by analyzing conceptual designs that comply with all critical owner and interconnection requirements and support RFQ specifications.

- Review conceptual project designs and validate compliance with applicable owner standards, utility interconnection requirements, and codes/standards.

- Prepare and validate electrical load lists and energy calculations (auxiliary power, station service, cable sizing, losses, and related studies inputs).

- Conduct thorough design reviews of electrical deliverables (drawings, technical specifications, and studies) including Balance of Plant, switchyard, and transmission line interconnection.

- Define the scope of all required electrical system studies (e.g., short circuit, arc flash, protection coordination, grounding, harmonic, and dynamic studies as applicable) and review results for accuracy and compliance.

- Track design schedules, update stakeholders, and ensure critical electrical engineering milestones and deadlines are met.

- Coordinate with operations engineering to incorporate lessons learned into new design reviews and specifications to continuously improve quality.

- Coordinate information and resolve technical interfaces between equipment suppliers, EPC/construction contractors, utilities, and the Engineer of Record.

- Support project close-out by organizing and transferring all as-built documentation to the final project owner including electrical drawings, schematics, bill of materials, electrical studies, and relay settings.

Procurement and Construction Support

- Provide procurement technical support, including preparation of specifications, vendor evaluations, support for technical RFPs, review of technical offers and shop drawings, and participation in factory visits and FAT inspections for major electrical equipment.

- Review competitive bids for owner-procured electrical material; support purchasing and manage suppliers throughout the engineering and commissioning process.

Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.

This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.

Job Description

Position Overview
The Thermal Asset Manager is responsible for a wide range of activities all directed toward the same goal: safely maximizing the profitability of Invenergy’s portfolio of operating thermal assets.

Responsibilities:
Operations:

- Coordinate with site-based and corporate O&M staff to optimize thermal asset performance, including major component repair and optimization of maintenance planning

- Evaluate and improve operational performance, including output, efficiency, and reliability, alongside engineering teams

- Participate in contract development with outside vendors, from soliciting quotes to supporting final contract negotiation

- Lead dispute negotiations if they arise with contractual counterparts

Finance:

- Develop annual budgets and perform periodic variance analyses for financial metrics such as EBITDA, distributions, etc.

- Provide input and review of the pro-forma financial models for generation assets

- Develop reports on generation asset performance for investors and lenders

- Assist in cash flow forecasting and management

- Perform financial analyses of aftermarket improvements, including profits, losses, and associated risks

- Develop other ad-hoc analyses as needed, coordinating with Accounting, Finance, Tax, etc.

Commercial:

- Provide input on optimizing the bidding and scheduling of assets in the market

- Support development and review commercial contracts and bids

- Collaborate with Commercial team on near-term and long-term power market strategy

Regulatory and compliance:

- Ensure compliance with the regulatory requirements and project agreements, including Power Purchase Agreements, Operating Agreements, Credit Agreements, and Operations and Maintenance Agreements

Required Skills

- Bachelor's Degree in Engineering

- 8+ years of experience in a similar function and industry, including but not limited to finance, accounting, FP&A, commercial management, project management, and consulting in industries such as energy, utilities, construction, manufacturing and real estate required

- Operational and/or engineering experience in thermal or an adjacent energy sector (cogeneration plants, gas turbines, steam turbines, etc.)

- Experience with standard financial metrics and analyses (NPV, IRR, DCF models)

- Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Excel

- Some travel required

- Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future

Preferred Skills

- Strong analytical, logical, and problem-solving skills

- Master’s Degree in Business, Economics, Finance, or Engineering

- Provide day-to-day engineering support for ICMS remanufacturing and drivetrain manufacturing activities.

- Support development, maintenance, and improvement of rebuild and assembly procedures, inspection requirements, and quality checkpoints.

- Participate in root cause analysis (RCA) and non-conformance investigations and support implementation of corrective actions for component, process, or manufacturing issues.

- Analyze inspection data, manufacturing reports, and repair outcomes to identify trends and support continuous improvement efforts.

- Work with Quality and operations teams to define and support inspection standards, documentation requirements, and traceability expectations.

- Assist in identifying gaps in procedures, training, or execution and support development of standardized solutions.

- Assist in development and validation of component acceptance criteria, tolerances, and fit/function requirements

- Support vendor performance evaluation through review of quality metrics, inspection data, and repair outcomes.

- Contribute to development of engineering documentation, including procedures, work instructions, and drawing updates as needed.

- Support engineering lab activities including CMM usage, measurement analysis, reverse engineering, and basic CAD/drawing support.

- Provide input to safety and risk evaluations, including fixtures, tooling, and handling processes, in coordination with EHS.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Operations, Asset Management, Quality, EHS, vendors, and other engineering groups.

- Support onboarding of new platforms, manufacturing processes, and repower-related activities at ICMS.

- Some travel and occasional field support may be required.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering or related technical discipline (or equivalent experience).

- 2+ years of relevant experience in manufacturing engineering, operations engineering, reliability engineering, or related field.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with ability to support technical troubleshooting and root cause analysis.

- Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and inspection data.

- Effective communication skills and ability to work with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Ability to manage multiple priorities and support projects with moderate guidance.

- Proficient in Microsoft Office tools.

- Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.

- Valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record.

Preferred Skills

- Experience with wind turbine components, drivetrain systems, or remanufacturing processes.

- Familiarity with manufacturing process tools, quality systems, inspection processes, or quality documentation (pFMEAs, control plans, NCRs).

- Experience working with CMM equipment or measurement tools.

- Experience with CAD software and creation or interpretation of engineering drawings.

- Familiarity with data analysis tools and systems (Excel, PowerBI, Python, etc.).

- Experience working with vendors, suppliers, or third-party manufacturing partners.

Job Description

The Quality Coordinator is a senior individual contributor role responsible for fleet wide governance and quality assurance of Incident Management and Process/Product Nonconformance programs, while also owning site specific quality process execution and improvement activities at the Invenergy Central Machine Shop.

This role serves as the Quality system steward for incident investigations and nonconformance governance across the fleet, ensuring consistent application of risk based rigor, investigation quality, and corrective action effectiveness in accordance with Invenergy policy and procedures. In parallel, the role provides hands on quality process leadership at the Central Machine Shop, supporting manufacturing, repair, inspection, and continuous improvement activities.

The Quality Coordinator operates as a technical authority, governance facilitator, and cross functional partner, not as a people manager.

- Maintain Intelex as the authoritative system of record, enforcing discipline in documentation, approvals, rationale, corrective actions, and evidence to ensure transparency, traceability, and audit readiness.

- Analyze fleet wide trends, repeat issues, and systemic weaknesses related to incidents and nonconformances; elevate insights and recommendations to the Director of Quality to support continuous improvement and preventive actions.

- Own site level quality process execution at the Central Machine Shop, including identification and documentation of process or product deviations, support of investigations, and verification of corrective action completion for shop specific issues.

- Partner with Machine Shop leadership, Engineering, Operations, and EHS to improve process consistency, inspection effectiveness, and defect prevention, translating fleet level lessons learned into practical local process improvements.
